m6_holdout_global_prior_finding_2026-09-: While verifying (not assuming) WHY the multihop witness's evidence improved holdout Brier, discovered a much broader structural fact affecting every M6/M7 calibration number this project has ever reported, including the original already-VALIDATED M6 v0.2 baseline (holdout Brier=0.48125, closed 2026-09-17): StructuralLearningPolicy.predict() has NEVER used BASIS_EXACT_BUCKET or BASIS_RULE_ONLY on any holdout evaluation -- 100% of holdout predictions fall back to BASIS_GLOBAL_PRIOR. Root cause, structural and by design (not a bug): split_by_rule() guarantees a rule never appears in both train and holdout, so a holdout record's rule signature is never present in the trained policy's bucket/rule counts. Consequence: every Brier/ECE number this project has reported measures whether the GLOBAL training class-frequency prior generalizes to new rules -- never rule-specific learning, despite the module's name and stated goal (Rule x Context x Depth x Provenance -> distribution). This does NOT invalidate the third-party validations (which always explicitly scoped their claims to mechanism honesty/reproducibility, never to rule-specific generalization -- see each protocol's 'Scientific non-closure' section) but corrects the informal reading of these Brier numbers as demonstrating structural learning. The initial hypothesis offered for the multihop witness's improvement ('same bias reproduces identically in train and holdout of the same rule') was checked directly and found to be STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE (confirmed false, not just superseded) -- the real, verified mechanism is a shift in the GLOBAL prior only. Verified robust-ness across 10 random splits: the multihop addition improves Brier in 8/10 seeds and WORSENS it in 2/10 -- not a guaranteed, causal improvement, a statistical tendency tied to how well the shifted prior happens to match a given holdout's composition. 3 new permanent tests (tests/test_m6_holdout_basis_diagnosis_v0_1.py) document this as CURRENT state (not enforced as a permanent invariant, since a future richer corpus reaching rule-specific holdout evaluation would be a genuine improvement, not a regression). 441/441 tests passing, zero regression. See documentation/MetaHIA_M6_Structural_Learning_V0_1.md Sec.11 and documentation/MetaHIA_M7_TextClaimParser_V0_1.md Sec.14 (corrected).

Also observed and disclosed: the golden check and the corpus builder call Ollama separately (no caching) for the same sentence and got a different answer on at least one case -- this small local model is not perfectly stable run-to-run at default temperature. A console-encoding mojibake artifact in the diagnostic script's stdout was investigated and ruled out as a real bug (verified the corpus file's UTF-8 bytes directly; ollama_generate_json's payload uses json.dumps(ensure_ascii=True).encode('utf-8'), independent of console encoding). 11 deterministic invariant tests + 1 skippable live demo. 385/385 tests passing, zero regression. Status: IMPLEMENTATION, not yet third-party validated. See documentation/MetaHIA_M7_TextClaimParser_V0_1.md.
m7_mixed_corpus_promotion_2026-09-18: Answers the load-bearing question raised before choosing the next M7 step (over length>1 extension or third-party validation): does feeding M7's LLM evidence into the SAME M6 promotion pipeline as the adversarial-corpus evidence help, hurt, or leave holdout calibration unchanged? m7_corpus_mixed_v0_1.py unions m6_corpus_from_m4_m5_v0_2.build_real_corpus_v2() (26 records, GROUNDED_DIRECT) with m7_corpus_from_llm_v0_1.build_llm_witnessed_corpus() (16 records, GROUNDED_ANALOGY, all still 16/16 CONTRADICTED as in the 2026-09-17 result) into one combined corpus fed unchanged through split_by_rule/StructuralLearningPolicy/evaluate_promotion. Fairness verified: the LLM mechanism can only add records for rules already present in the adversarial corpus, so split_by_rule assigns the identical holdout rule set under the same seed in both runs -- a genuine same-holdout comparison. Real result (llama3.2:latest, seed=0, brier_threshold=0.5): baseline (adversarial only) holdout Brier=0.48125/ECE=0.025, train=16/holdout=5, PROMOTE; mixed (adversarial+LLM) holdout Brier=0.47/ECE=0.025, train=25/holdout=8, PROMOTE. Honest reading: the Brier movement (0.48125->0.47) is small on a 5-8 record holdout and cannot be credited to genuine LLM analogical skill given its evidence is itself systematically CONTRADICTED regardless of ground truth -- conclusion is calibration-NEUTRAL at current scale/model, not a demonstrated improvement, and does not yet justify further investment (length>1 extension, third-party validation) ahead of improving the LLM's individual accuracy or growing the corpus. See MetaHIA_M7_LLM_Fact_Proposer_V0_1.md Sec.6. 364/364 tests passing, zero regression.
